newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end lower after Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end lower after Greenspan comments.

text.p: Swedish shares ended lower on Wednesday after diving when U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan voiced concerns about skyrocketing U.S. stock prices and the risk of higher inflation.
The exchange's general index fell 0.13 percent to 2,663.16 in turnover of 5.80 billion crowns.
But dealers did not think the bourse's upward trend would be broken by Greenspan's comments.

"It seems like there is too much money on too few markets," a trader said. "Today it was 'Greenspan - so what?.' Then money from bonds will come into the market in March and this might have a positive effect."
"But there are several classical signs that this market should calm down," he said, adding he did not think it would.
Drugs major Pharmacia & Upjohn PNU.ST dropped seven crowns to 275 after releasing 1996 earnings and later saying it may not meet its goal of a 25 percent operating profit margin by 1998.
But rival Astra rose, up three to 363. It benefited from shareholders in mortage bank Stadshypotek cashing in money from new owner Handelsbanken.
Dealers said shareholders put this money into Astra, telecoms group Ericsson and automotive group Volvo. Ericsson rose two to 241.5 and Volvo edged up 0.5 to 184.5.
Banking group Nordbanken plummeted six to 268 crowns after coming off day highs of 280. Earlier in the day the share rose on a newspaper article saying a foreign bank was interested in buying it.
